tagline: Bridge Jira development tracking with ClickUp product planning
metaTitle: Jira ClickUp Integration: Two-Way Story and Task Sync
metaDescription: Sync Jira story status to ClickUp tasks and create Jira stories from ClickUp features. GAIA maps the hierarchy and priorities. See the setup steps.
intro:
Product teams that plan and track delivery in ClickUp often run into a wall when engineering uses Jira for day-to-day development. Each team has legitimate reasons for their tool preference, but the boundary between them creates a coordination overhead that neither team should have to manage manually. Status updates made by engineers do not appear on the delivery board. Requirements changed by product managers do not reach the engineers' stories.

GAIA bridges Jira and ClickUp by syncing the relevant data in both directions automatically. Engineering progress flows to the product delivery board. Product requirement changes propagate to the corresponding stories. Both teams work in their preferred tool and trust that the other side stays current.

This integration is particularly valuable for organizations that have standardized on one tool for company-wide project management but let engineering use the other for its superior development tooling — Agile boards, sprint planning, and deep Atlassian ecosystem integrations.

useCases.title: Sync Jira story status to ClickUp tasks
useCases.description: When a story moves to In Progress or Done, GAIA updates the linked task status so product managers always see accurate development progress on their delivery boards without polling engineers.

useCases.title: Create stories from ClickUp feature tasks
useCases.description: When a feature task is approved and moved to Ready for Development, GAIA creates a corresponding story with the task description, acceptance criteria, and priority already populated.

useCases.title: Propagate priority changes to Jira
useCases.description: When a product manager changes a task priority, for example, upgrading a feature from Medium to Critical, GAIA updates the priority of the linked story and notifies the assigned engineer so they can adjust their sprint queue.

useCases.title: Sync sprint dates to milestones
useCases.description: GAIA reads Jira sprint start and end dates and creates or updates corresponding ClickUp milestones, keeping the product delivery timeline aligned with actual engineering sprints.

useCases.title: Surface blockers for product managers
useCases.description: When a story is marked as blocked, GAIA adds a comment to the linked task summarizing the blocker so product managers can take cross-team action without waiting for engineering stand-up.

howItWorks.step: Connect Jira and ClickUp to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your Jira project and ClickUp workspace. Map projects to Spaces and Folders during initial configuration.

howItWorks.step: Define field mappings and sync direction
howItWorks.description: Map workflow statuses to task statuses, define which fields are authoritative in which tool, and configure which events should trigger cross-platform actions.
GAIA monitors both sides for relevant changes and propagates updates in real time. Product managers and engineers each work in their own tool, and both boards always reflect the same current state.

faqs.question: How does GAIA handle the Jira epic-story-subtask hierarchy versus ClickUp's task-subtask model?
faqs.answer: GAIA maps epics to tasks and stories to subtasks by default, or you can map each level to a separate hierarchy tier. The mapping is configurable to match your team's organizational conventions.

faqs.question: Can GAIA sync custom fields?
faqs.answer: Yes. During setup you map custom fields on one side to their counterparts on the other. GAIA handles type conversion — for example, mapping a number field to a numeric field — and logs any fields that cannot be mapped cleanly.

faqs.question: What happens to tasks that have no corresponding story?
faqs.answer: GAIA only syncs tasks that match your configured rules — typically tasks that have been explicitly linked or that match a trigger like being moved to a Ready for Development list. Unlinked tasks are left untouched.
